overall: The AG found the Select Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law as alleged: the notice omitted a topic the chair could not reasonably anticipate 48 hours ahead. Town policy claims were declined.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the January 7 meeting notice was not specific enough because it omitted a statement the Town Administrator read aloud about the Board of Assessors.
allegations.key_passage: its omission does not render the meeting notice insufficiently specific.

allegations.summary: Complainant argued the statement should have been read in executive session rather than open session.
allegations.key_passage: A public body is not required to convene an executive session to discuss any particular topic.

allegations.summary: Complainant argued she should have been invited to the meeting to respond to the statement read about her position.
allegations.key_passage: the Open Meeting Law does not require specific notice to an individual unless a public body plans to convene in executive session under Purpose 1

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged violation of town policies, which the AG said falls outside the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: to the extent that the complainant alleges a violation of town policies, that allegation falls outside of the Open Meeting Law and we therefore decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Board argued it did not deliberate on the topic; the subsequent vote to schedule a joint meeting with the Board of Assessors was raised as possible deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: Arguably, the vote itself could constitute deliberation.
